posts.title: Being Too Professional About Hobby Projects
posts.description: I had never received formal training in software engineering. I majored in nanomaterials in college. I went to grad school in data science. My first research assistant job was with a business school, and my papers were in social psychology. I had never studied software engineering or computer science. Yet my first full-time job was as a software engineer at Google. The imposter syndrome was real.

posts.title: Backpacks that carried me
posts.description: The travelers There was this backpack. It was technically my dad’s; I just kept borrowing it. I took it to England while I was 14, to western China later in high school, and to northern India during college. I don’t even remember the brand; to me, it’s just the travel bag . posts.title: Rolling Dice on a $60 handheld
posts.description: In the last post, “ Porting Raylib to a $60 GBA clone ”, I described how I convinced Raylib to draw 3D scenes on a budget handheld — the Miyoo Mini Flip (MMF) — that has no GPU whatsoever. The trick was pairing Raylib’s bare-framebuffer platform (PLATFORM_MEMORY) with TinyGL , a software OpenGL 1.1 renderer that skips the expensive glReadPixels copy step.
